pages.text: Tina is a sea turtle. She has a hard shell on her back that helps protect her in the ocean.
Tina swims with strong flippers. Flippers flap like paddles and help her glide through water smoothly.
Even though Tina lives in water, she must breathe air. She swims up and takes a breath at the surface.
Tina loves seagrass and jellyfish. She eats slowly and carefully, using her mouth to bite and chew.
Sometimes Tina sees floating plastic. Plastic can look like food, but it can hurt ocean animals badly.
Tina swims away from trash. A clean ocean is safer for turtles, fish, and every sea creature.
When it is time, Tina visits a sandy beach. Sea turtles lay eggs on beaches, not underwater.
Tina digs a nest with her flippers. She lays eggs and covers them with sand to keep them warm.
Weeks later, baby turtles hatch. They crawl toward the ocean and begin their first swim.
Tina returns to the sea, breathing air, swimming strong, and reminding us: keep oceans clean and safe.
